sections.value: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language models by grounding their responses in external knowledge. Instead of relying solely on pre-trained weights, RAG retrieves relevant documents at query time and uses them as context for generation. This reduces hallucination and keeps outputs up to date with your data.
The diagram below illustrates the typical RAG workflow: from user query to retrieval, context assembly, and final answer generation.

sections.alt: RAG workflow diagram showing retrieval and generation pipeline

sections.value: Key steps include: (1) encoding the query into an embedding, (2) searching a vector store for relevant chunks, (3) combining retrieved passages with the query, and (4) generating a response using the LLM conditioned on that context. Fine-tuning retrieval and generation jointly can further improve end-to-end quality.
